vulnerabilityAlerts.description: The security label is not decoration: the dependency watchdog identifies a security pull request by this label plus Renovate authorship, and matching on the title instead produced nineteen false positives elsewhere in the fleet. Renovate's own defaults already let a vulnerability fix bypass the release-age gate and the schedule, which is why neither is restated here.

lockFileMaintenance.description: Rewrite dashboard/package-lock.json and uv.lock from scratch every week so transitive dependencies pick up published fixes. Ordinary updates only touch the entries named in a manifest, so an advisory against a package no manifest names is never resolved until the lockfile itself is refreshed. Renovate's minimumReleaseAge filters the versions Renovate proposes, but here the package manager picks every version. For npm, min-release-age=7 in dashboard/.npmrc makes npm refuse anything younger than seven days, which is what makes automerge safe for the dashboard lockfile. uv.lock gets its own branch and is not automerged, see the rule for it below. This is a public repository, so the run costs nothing.

customManagers.description: The source-only job runs one leg per supported Python minor, listed under strategy.matrix.python-version in .github/workflows/ci.yml. The github-actions manager reads only literal setup-python inputs, so this extracts each matrix entry with the datasource, package and version format that manager uses for setup-python.

mcr-playwright.description: Microsoft Artifact Registry's tag catalog for mcr.microsoft.com/playwright. Every vX.Y.Z-noble tag, the scheme the CI container pins, becomes a release with the catalog's lastModifiedDate, the time MCR last pushed that tag, as its release timestamp and the tag's current manifest-list digest. Other distributions, architecture tags and the bare vX.Y.Z tags are left out.

packageRules.description: setup-python takes its version from the job matrix, which the github-actions manager cannot resolve and would report as an invalid version. The python-matrix custom manager updates the matrix entries instead.

Each python-matrix entry is the CI leg of one supported Python minor, so it takes only patch releases of its own minor. separateMinorPatch gives each entry its own patch branch (python-3.14.x, python-3.15.x); without it, the newest minor is the only proposal, an older leg never receives its patch releases, and accepting the proposal would move that leg to a minor it does not represent. A new minor arrives through the requires-python rule instead. The entries hold release numbers with no place for a digest, as with the uses-with inputs below.
Moving a python-matrix entry to another minor would stop testing the minor it represents while requires-python still declares it.

Renovate's docker datasource reads release timestamps only from Docker Hub, so under timestamp-required every update of the Playwright CI container would stay pending. The image is looked up through the mcr-playwright datasource instead, which dates each tag and digest with the time MCR pushed it, so the seven-day wait applies to it too.

The version inputs of setup-uv and setup-node (depType uses-with) take a release number and have no place for a commit digest. With pinDigests, Renovate proposes 'Pin dependency astral-sh/uv to <digest>', which fails on every run with 'update failure'. For node it looks for a git tag named exactly after the release, finds none because actions/node-versions adds a build number to every tag, logs 'Could not determine new digest for update' and drops the update without telling anyone, so Node would never be updated.
Public repository: merge eligible non-major updates after checks pass. Group only dependencies that need coordinated updates; keep unrelated updates separate.

requires-python declares which Python minors this project supports, not which version to install, so the repository-wide rangeStrategy pin is wrong for it: an exact ==3.x.y would reject the next patch release, including one that fixes a vulnerability. widen only ever adds the new minor to the upper bound; replace would move the lower bound too and silently drop a supported minor. Supporting a new minor also needs a CI matrix leg and documentation, so the proposal is never automerged, and tests/test_release_compliance.py keeps it red until the matrix covers the new range.

Re-resolves uv.lock so transitive packages pick up upstream fixes that no direct-dependency rule reaches. Not automerged: uv has no package-manager-level release-age gate, so nothing holds back a package published yesterday when the lock file is rebuilt, and a human reads the diff instead. Its own branch keeps the automerged npm refresh from waiting on that review.
Majors land one at a time and are merged by a human after reading the migration notes. Public repository, so each major is proposed separately rather than bundled.
